title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 83-84
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 83 to 84 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'समावर्तोऽनिवृत्तात्मा दुर्जयो दुरतिक्रमः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 83 to 84 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 83 to 84.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 83 to 84** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **समावर्तोऽनिवृत्तात्मा दुर्जयो दुरतिक्रमः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**समावर्तोऽनिवृत्तात्मा दुर्जयो दुरतिक्रमः । दुर्लभो दुर्गमो दुर्गो दुरावासो दुरारिहा ॥** **शुभाङ्गो लोकसारङ्गः सुतन्तुस्तन्तुवर्धनः । इन्द्रकर्मा महाकर्मा कृतकर्मा कृतागमः ॥**

He returns in every age, his Self never turns back, hard to conquer and hard to cross is he. Hard to attain and hard to reach, a fortress and the one who scatters his foes, is that God of gods. Fair of limb, the essence of the worlds, the fine thread that he spins and lengthens. He does the works of Indra and great works; whatever he sets out to do, that God of gods completes.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 83 to 84 mean?
faq.a: He returns in every age, his Self never turns back, hard to conquer and hard to cross is he. Hard to attain and hard to reach, a fortress and the one who scatters his foes, is that God of gods. Fair of limb, the essence of the worlds, the fine thread that he spins and lengthens. He does the works of Indra and great works; whatever he sets out to do, that God of gods completes.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
